title: Epsilon Indi B — a pair of nearby brown dwarfs
plain_result: From SPHEREx positions (with Gaia's distance held fixed) we measured how fast it moves across the sky: +3.96 ± 0.07″ and -2.43 ± 0.07″ per year (east–west, north–south). ESA's Gaia measured +3.98″ and -2.47″.

numbers.label: Absorption bands found in its SPHEREx spectrum (water, methane, carbon monoxide)

method_note: Each picture is fitted with the star's position free, saturated pixels masked and Gaia neighbours modelled; the motion is a straight-line fit to SPHEREx positions with Gaia's parallax held fixed. This fit was not written down in advance. Positions sit a steady ~0.5″ south of Gaia's prediction in every survey; the pair is unresolved, so a shifted centre of light is possible — not explained here.

figures.alt: SPHEREx spectrum of Epsilon Indi B from 0.75 to 5 micrometres with water, methane and carbon monoxide bands marked
figures.caption: SPHEREx spectrum from 246 pictures. Grey strips: absorption bands that passed our pre-set test. Green: published brightness through standard filters.
